{{Notability|date=October 2023}}

{{Short description|American philosopher}}
'''Timothy Chambers''' is a [[philosopher]] who has written a number of articles which have appeared in the journals ''Mind,'' the ''Monist'' (1998), ''Philosophy'' (2001), the ''Aristotelian Society Proceedings'' (2000), and ''Ratio'' (1999).  His research interests include [[Hilary Putnam]], [[time travel]], the [[Ontological Argument]], the [[Doomsday Argument]] and the [[semantics]] of [[vagueness]].  His work on Putnam included a logical formula—the Chambers Conditional<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wright |first=C |title=On being in a quandary. Relativism vagueness logical revisionism |journal=Mind |volume=110 |issue=437 |pages=45–98 |year=2001 |doi=10.1093/mind/110.437.45 |url=http://mind.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/content/abstract/110/437/45 |access-date=2006-07-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070311013301/http://mind.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/content/abstract/110/437/45 |archive-date=2007-03-11 |url-status=dead |url-access=subscription }}</ref>—which figures in [[Crispin Wright]]'s recent work on vagueness.<ref>[http://www.philosophy.ox.ac.uk/faculty/members/docs/inaugural.pdf]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061006170748/http://www.philosophy.ox.ac.uk/faculty/members/docs/inaugural.pdf|date=October 6, 2006}}</ref><ref>[http://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/philosophy/arche/pages/papers/Wright%20Liars%20and%20Heaps.pdf] {{dead link|date=June 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
